implementation_notes: C# has a genuine local idiom for the case you cannot move the method into the data class — the extension method — but it is a partial cure: it makes the operation discoverable at the call site while the knowledge still lives outside the type. Use it when the data type is sealed, owned by another team, or a framework type you must not change; otherwise prefer a real member. ReSharper/Rider and the built-in analyzers will not flag feature envy by default, so the practical detector is a search for repeated property-getter runs across the solution.
idiom_name: extension method used as a substitute for Move Method
pitfalls: Extension methods proliferate into a second, invisible API surface for a type; they are a fallback, not the default answer.
A LINQ query chain over another object's properties is envy expressed as an expression tree, and is usually better left as a query.
Records and `init`-only types invite the assumption that the rule belongs somewhere else; the rule still needs a home.
